To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we purified four proteins with RACK-like properties from rat hepatocytes.
we purified several RACKs (receptors for activated protein kinase) from rat hepatocytes and that these RACKs are likely to be involved in protein kinase C signaling in hepatocytes.
we have isolated and partially characterized several proteins from rat liver that share the properties of being precipitated with Tritons and binding protein kinase C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of proteins that interact with activated protein kinase C.
the identification, purification and characterization of proteins that interact with PKC.
the identification and characterization of RACKs in rat hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these four proteins are not identical to each other and they may be different RACKs or other proteins that share the ability to interact with activated protein kinase C.
these proteins are novel, distinct, and unique RACKs that are present in hepatocytes.
the RACKs are a group of proteins that share the ability of interacting with activated protein kinase C, and that they are not homologues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RACKs are proteins that are not only involved in the anchoring of protein kinase C, but are also involved in other cellular functions.
we isolated and purified a group of proteins that are able to be precipitated by Triton X- 100 and that may be RACKs for protein kinase C. These
RACKs are a family of proteins with a broad tissue distribution that share common characteristics and may have similar functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RACKs purified here are not identical to RACK1 and RACK2 previously identified in brain and other tissues.
a number of RACK proteins are present in rat hepatocytes.
the method described herein can be used to isolate proteins that are associated with the cytoskeleton and/or the plasma membrane.
